packages.angle: Every single character with a stake in Elbaf begged Luffy not to free Loki -- he did it anyway, confirmed via real episode 1171 reviews (aired July 26, 2026), not manga or trailer coverage.
hook_candidates: Every person around Loki told Luffy not to do this.
One Piece just freed the giant every giant on the island wanted locked up forever.
packages.hook_line: Every person around Loki told Luffy not to do this.
packages.opening_sentence: Every person around Loki told Luffy not to do this.
packages.vo: Every person around Loki told Luffy not to do this. Hajrudin called him manipulative and cruel, Sanji tried to physically stop it, and Zoro stayed on guard the whole time, but Luffy freed him anyway. Episode 1171 doesn't even give Loki a fight to earn that trust, because the moment he stands up, chains gone and weapon in hand, every character just freezes while the music slowly builds instead. That freeze is the tell: nobody in that scene believed freeing him was safe, yet nobody moved to stop him either. Is Loki about to prove the warnings right, or prove Luffy's instinct right instead? Leave your take.
packages.question_line: Is Loki about to prove the warnings right, or prove Luffy's instinct right instead?

claim_source_matrix.claim: Hajrudin desperately begs Luffy not to free Loki, warning him that Loki is manipulative, cruel, and capable of fooling anyone who shows him sympathy.
Hajrudin, Sanji, and the New Giant Warrior Pirates rush toward the Underworld in a desperate attempt to stop Luffy before it is too late.
Zoro refuses to ignore Loki's terrible reputation and remains cautious from the very beginning; Zoro argues with Luffy over freeing Loki and does not trust him.
Luffy and Zoro free Loki; by the time Hajrudin's group arrives, the chains have already been removed.
Despite suffering terrible injuries, Loki slowly rises to his feet and reaches for his massive weapon, Ragnir -- no fight occurs on screen, the episode ends on this standing moment.

The scene is built on silence and mounting music rather than action: every character freezes as Loki stands, the music gradually builds, and the atmosphere shifts from hopeful to unsettling; the episode wisely stops before any battle.
Episode 1171 aired July 26, 2026, per the official One Piece episode release calendar.

packages.angle: Eri's Quirk could erase people from existence -- the new special 'I Am a Hero Too' gives her the opposite: a guitar and a concert her heroes watch in secret, confirmed via the Anime Expo premiere review and independent fan viewing accounts.
hook_candidates: My Hero Academia just gave the girl who could erase people a guitar instead.
packages.vo: Eri's Quirk was called Rewind. It could erase a person entirely, undo them back to nothing. That was the power Overhaul tortured her for. In My Hero Academia: I Am a Hero Too, Eri doesn't use that power at all. She picks up a guitar instead. The special centers on her first concert, mentored by Jiro and Kaminari, with Deku and Mirio watching in secret so attention stays on her. A girl whose defining power was undoing things chose the one skill that only builds forward. That's the actual arc, a rewrite of what her power meant. Does that change how you see her Quirk? Leave your take.

claim_source_matrix.claim: Eri's Quirk is named Rewind and can rewind a living being's body, including reverting people back to a point before they existed -- effectively erasing them from existence.
The villain Overhaul experimented on and tortured Eri to study and exploit her Rewind Quirk.

In the new special 'My Hero Academia: I Am a Hero Too,' an older Eri has formed her own street band and performs a cover of 'Hero Too' as her debut concert -- she does not use her Quirk in this special.
Jiro and Kaminari have taken Eri under their wing, fostering her love of music and mentoring her toward this concert.
Deku and Mirio (now famous heroes) attend Eri's concert but must stay hidden from the crowd so the attention remains on Eri, not on them.
